summary.text: Ashley Moody is the incumbent Republican U.S. Senator from Florida. A Plant City native and University of Florida graduate, she worked as a lawyer and federal prosecutor, served as a Hillsborough County circuit judge, and was elected Florida Attorney General in 2018 and 2022 before Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed her to the Senate in January 2025. She is running to serve the remainder of Marco Rubio's term, which expires in January 2029.

paragraphs.text: Ashley Moody was born in Plant City, Florida, in 1975, and her Senate biography describes her as a fifth-generation Floridian.

She earned bachelor's and master's degrees in accounting (1993 and 1996) and a J.D. (2000) from the University of Florida, and an LL.M. in international law from Stetson University College of Law in 2010.

Moody began her legal career at the law firm Holland & Knight, practicing commercial litigation, and then served as an assistant U.S. attorney for the Middle District of Florida, prosecuting drug, firearm and fraud offenses; she was also an adjunct professor at Stetson University College of Law.

In 2006 she was elected to the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit Court in Hillsborough County at age 31, which her Senate biography describes as making her the youngest judge in Florida, and she served on the bench from 2007 to 2017.
Moody won the 2018 election for Florida Attorney General, 52.1% to 46.1% over Sean Shaw, and was re-elected in 2022, 60.6% to 39.4% over Aramis Ayala; she served from 2019 to 2025.

According to her Senate biography, as Attorney General she served on the Presidential Commission on Law Enforcement and the Administration of Justice during the first Trump administration and chaired Florida's Statewide Council on Human Trafficking, and the biography also cites the state's share of opioid litigation settlements.
Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed her to succeed Marco Rubio after he became Secretary of State, and she was sworn into the U.S. Senate on January 21, 2025.

She serves on the Judiciary, Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, and Health, Education, Labor and Pensions committees, the Special Committee on Aging and the Joint Economic Committee. Her Senate biography says she and her husband, Justin, a career law enforcement officer, have two sons.
